messages:
Sarah C.: heads up — getting a pile of CS tickets saying API calls are getting 429s + occasional 401 during a marketing burst. started ~08:13 UTC. customers report 'quota exceeded' even though their dashboard shows headroom.
Ben O.: on it. which pool/tenant? any correlation with model version?
Sarah C.: looks like multiple tenants across the us-west-2 cluster. mainly for text-gen v1 and embedding v2. dashboard spikes in 'request_rejected' for the burst-handler limiter rule.
Maria G.: seeing same in logs: limiter_meter shows tokens_in_window hitting hard cap then immediate rejections. interestingly refill_rate shows 0 for some windows.
Leo P.: 0 refill_rate? that sounds like a config push. did we deploy limiter config change in the last 24h?
eng-sre-bot: deploy: limiter-config-service v3.4.1 rolled to staging 05:42 UTC, canary to us-west-2 started 07:50 UTC, completed 08:02 UTC.
Sarah C.: timeline matches. ops-bot: can you map which shards got the canary?
ops-bot: canary targeted shards: s3,s7,s8 in us-west-2. rollback flag available at /ops/flags/limiter-canary.
Ben O.: grabbing logs from s7.
Ben O.: log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z WARN limiter: bucket_size=0 refill_rate=0 tenant=acme-corp route=/v1/generate
2026-03-15T08:10:12Z ERROR limiter: reject request quota_exceeded tenant=acme-corp request_id=abcd-1234
```
Maria G.: that bucket_size=0 is a smoking gun. config should never set bucket_size to 0; default is >=1. maybe a YAML parse bug transformed "null" into 0?
Leo P.: checking config repo commit history... https://git.redwood/ops/limiter-config/commit/7a9f1e. recent change introduced `burst_capacity: ${env.BURST_CAPACITY:-0}` to support opt-in. env var missing in our canary deployment.
Sarah C.: so canary without env var -> burst_capacity 0 -> immediate rejections under concurrent load. :facepalm:
Ben O.: mitigation options: 1) roll back limiter-config-service to v3.4.0 (fast), 2) flip canary env var via k8s patch to set BURST_CAPACITY=1000, 3) add temporary route-level bypass for known enterprise customers. thoughts?
Maria G.: rollback is safest and quick. patching live env var could work but risk of drift. route bypass is heavier ops and exposes us to abuse.
Leo P.: I'm in favor of rollback. preparing deploy rollback to 3.4.0 now.
eng-sre-bot: action queued: rollback limiter-config-service on shards s3,s7,s8. estimated completion 2m.
Ben O.: pushing emergency notice to CS: "we're rolling back a configuration change affecting rate limiting; expect intermittent 429s to subside within ~5 minutes".
Sarah C.: CS updated. I'm fielding top-priority customers; they want ETA and root cause — be succinct: config canary omitted env var causing burst capacity to be zero.
ops-bot: rollback completed on s3,s7,s8 at 08:15:18Z. health checks green.
Ben O.: monitoring token rejection metric now... looks like rejections dropping back to baseline.
Maria G.: confirmed. refill_rate and bucket_size restored to expected values.
Leo P.: creating postmortem checklist: how did BURST_CAPACITY env var not exist in canary? why didn't our integration tests catch this?
Sarah C.: immediate follow-ups: 1) temp mitigate — done (rollback). 2) customer outreach — on it. 3) revert canary config change and add gating — action items below.
Ben O.: repro steps for QA to validate fix before re-deploy:
1. create a small test tenant.
2. set BURST_CAPACITY unset and deploy v3.4.1 to canary shard.
3. run 200 concurrent requests simulating marketing spike: `wrk -t10 -c200 -d30s http://canary-shard/v1/generate`
4. assert no 429s and bucket_size >= 1.

Include this in the runbook.
Maria G.: adding unit/integration test: config template must be validated by schema that disallows 0 for burst_capacity; default to 100 when env missing. will open PR.
Leo P.: also adding CI check: when deploying limiter-config-service, ensure env var set or template uses safe default. if missing, fail the deploy.
Sarah C.: CS list of affected customers — sending post-rollback note and offer to help with throttling settings. keep legal looped for any SLA implications.
ops-bot: filed incident ticket INC-20260315-42, severity: P2, assignees: eng-sre, oncall. link: https://redwood/incidents/INC-20260315-42
Ben O.: quick note: billing showed no overcharges — rejection happens before token accounting increments, so customers weren't billed for rejected tokens.
Maria G.: follow-up action items (short):
- [ ] PR: add schema validation for burst_capacity (owner: Maria G.)
- [ ] CI gating for env presence on canary (owner: Leo P.)
- [ ] Runbook update with rollback/playbook steps (owner: Ben O.)
- [ ] Customer communication templates and CS brief (owner: Sarah C.)
- [ ] Postmortem write-up and RCA (owner: eng-sre oncall)

Sarah C.: I'll schedule a quick 30m sync with CS + eng-sre in 1 hour to review comms and timelines. thanks team — good catch and fast rollback. :clap:
eng-sre-bot: incident INC-20260315-42 status -> mitigated. next update in 24h or on request.
Leo P.: closing thread for now, moving action items into the incident board. if anything else pops up, re-open here.
Sarah C.: noted. leaving ticket open until postmortem completed.
